nodes.name: \[(\epsilon, \kappa)\]-closeness
nodes.statement: A dictionary \[bA\] is \[(epsilon, kappa)\]-close to \[bA^*\] if \[\|bA - bA^*\| leq kappa\|bA^*\|\], and if there is a permutation \[pi: [m] rightarrow [m]\] and a collection of signs \[sigma: [m] rightarrow \pm 1\\] such that \[\|sigma(i)bA_pi(i) - bA^*_i\|leq epsilon, ~forall~ iin [m]\].vspace-3pt
nodes.raw_latex:
\label{def:del_kappa}
\textit{A dictionary \[\b{A}\] is \[(\epsilon, \kappa)\]-close to \[\b{A}^*\] if \[\|\b{A} - \b{A}^*\| \leq \kappa\|\b{A}^*\|\], and if there is a permutation \[\pi: [m] \rightarrow [m]\] and a collection of signs \[\sigma: [m] \rightarrow \{\pm 1\}\] such that \[\|\sigma(i)\b{A}_{\pi(i)} - \b{A}^*_i\|\leq \epsilon, ~\forall~ i\in [m]\].}\vspace{-3pt}

nodes.name: Distribution class \[\c{D}\]
nodes.statement: The coefficient vector \[bx^*\] belongs to an unknown distribution \[cD\], where the support \[S = supp(bx^*)\] is at most of size \[k\], \[bPr[i in S] = Theta(k/m)\] and \[bPr[i, j in S] = Theta(k^2/m^2)\]. Moreover, the distribution is normalized such that \[bE[bx_i^*|i in S] = 0\] and \[bE[bx_i^*^2|i in S] = 1\], and when \[i in S\], \[|bx^*_i| geq C\] for some constant \[C leq 1\]. In addition, the non-zero entries are sub-Gaussian and pairwise independent conditioned on the support.

nodes.name: \textbf{Signed-support recovery by coefficient initialization step}
nodes.statement: Suppose \[bA^(t)\] is \[epsilon_t\]-close to \[bA^*\]. Then, if \[mu = cO(log(n))\], \[k = sqrtn/mulog(n)\], and \[epsilon_t = O^*(1/sqrtlog(m))\], with probability at least \[(1 - delta_cT^(t))\] for each random sample \[by = bA^*bx^*\]: sign(cT_C/2((bA^(t))^top by) = sign(bx^*), where \[delta_cT^(t) = 2m~exp(-tfracC^2O^*(epsilon_t^2))\].
conclusions: Then, if \[mu = cO(log(n))\], \[k = sqrtn/mulog(n)\], and \[epsilon_t = O^*(1/sqrtlog(m))\], with probability at least \[(1 - delta_cT^(t))\] for each random sample \[by = bA^*bx^*\]: sign(cT_C/2((bA^(t))^top by) = sign(bx^*), where \[delta_cT^(t) = 2m~exp(-tfracC^2O^*(epsilon_t^2))\].

This completes the proof of our main result.

nodes.statement: Let \[by in R^n\] be general sample generated as \[by = bA^*bx^*\], where \[bx^* in R^m\] is a sparse random vector with support \[S = supp(bx^*)\] distributed according to D.. The initial decoding step at the \[t\]-th iteration (shown in Algorithm~) involves evaluating the inner-product between the estimate of the dictionary \[bA^(t)\], and \[by\]. The \[i\]-th element of the resulting vector can be written as langle bA_i^(t), byrangle &= langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_i rangle bx^*_i + bw_i, where \[bw_i = langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_-ibx^*_-irangle \]. Now, since \[\|bA_i^* - bA^(t)_i\|_2 leq epsilon_t\] and \|bA_i^* - bA^(t)_i\|_2^2 &= \|bA_i^* \|^2 + \|bA^(t)_i\|^2 - 2langle bA^(t)_i, bA^*_i rangle = 2 - 2langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_i rangle, we have |langle bA^(t)_i, bA^*_i rangle| geq 1 - epsilon^2_t/2. Therefore, the term |langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_irangle bx^*_i| geq (1 - tfracepsilon_t^22)C &, if ~ i in S,\\ = 0&, otherwise. Now, we focus on the \[bw_i\] and show that it is small. By the definition of \[bw_i\] we have bw_i = langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_-ibx^*_-irangle = textstylesumlimits_ellneq ilangle bA^(t)_i, bA^*_ell rangle bx^*_ell = textstylesumlimits_ell in Sbackslash \i\langle bA^(t)_i, bA^*_ell rangle bx^*_ell. Here, since \[var(bx_ell^*) = 1\], \[bw_i\] is a zero-mean random variable with variance var(bw_i) = textstylesumlimits_ell in Sbackslash \i\langle bA^(t)_i, bA^*_ell rangle^2. Now, each term in this sum can be bounded as, langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_ell rangle^2 &= (langle bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle + langle bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle)^2\\ &leq 2(langle bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2 + langle bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2)\\ &leq 2(langle bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2 + tfracmu^2n). Next, \[textstylesumlimits_ellneq i langle bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2\] can be upper-bounded as &textstylesumlimits_ell in Sbackslash \i\ langle bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2 leq \|bA_Sbackslash\i\^*\|^2 epsilon_t^2. Therefore, we have the following as per our assumptions on \[mu\] and \[k\], \|bA_Sbackslash\i\^*\|^2 leq (1 + k tfracmusqrtn) leq 2, using Gershgorin Circle Theorem citepGershgorin1931. Therefore, we have textstylesumlimits_ell in Sbackslash \i\ langle bA^(t)_i - bA_i^*, bA^*_ellrangle^2 leq 2epsilon_t^2. Finally, we have that textstylesumlimits_ell in Sbackslash \i\langle bA_i^(t), bA^*_ell rangle^2 leq 2( 2epsilon^2_t + k tfracmu^2n) = O^*(epsilon_t^2). Now, we apply the Chernoff bound for sub-Gaussian random variables \[bw_i\] (shown in Lemma~) to conclude that Pr[|bw_i|geq C/4] leq 2exp(-tfracC^2 O^*(epsilon_t^2)). Further, \[bw_i\] corresponding to each \[m\] should follow this bound, applying union bound we conclude that Pr[ undersetimax~|bw_i| geq C/4] leq 2mexp(-tfracC^2O^*(epsilon_t^2)) := delta_cT^(t) .

nodes.statement: Consider the \[(r+1)\]-th iterate \[bx^(r+1)\] for the \[t\]-th dictionary iterate, where \[\|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|leq epsilon_t\] for all \[i in [1, m]\] evaluated as the following by the update step described in Algorithm~, bx^(r+1) &= bx^(r) - eta_x^(r+1)bA^(t)^top(bA^(t)bx^(r) - by) notag\\ &= (bI - eta_x^(r+1)bA^(t)^topbA^(t))bx^(r) - eta_x^(r+1)bA^(t)^topbA^*bx^*, where \[eta_x^(1) < 1\] is the learning rate or the step-size parameter. Now, using Lemma~ we know that \[bx^(0)\] has the correct signed-support with probability at least \[(1-delta_cT^(t))\]. Further, since \[bA^(t)^topbA^*\] can be written as bA^(t)^topbA^* = (bA^(t)- bA^*)^topbA^* + bA^*topbA^*, we can write the \[(r+1)\]-th iterate of the coefficient update step using as bx^(r+1) &= (bI - eta_x^(r+1)bA^(t)^topbA^(t))bx^(r) - eta_x^(r+1) (bA^(t) -bA^*)^topbA^*bx^* + eta_x^(r+1) bA^*topbA^*bx^*. Further, the \[j\]-th entry of this vector is given by bx^(r+1)_j hspace-3pt= hspace-3pt(bI - eta_x^(r+1) bA^(t)^tophspace-3ptbA^(t))_(j,:)bx^(r) - eta_x^(r+1) &((bA^(t) - bA^*)^tophspace-3ptbA^*)_(j,:)bx^* hspace-3pt+hspace-3pt eta_x^(r+1)(bA^*tophspace-3ptbA^*)_(j,:)bx^*. We now develop an expression for the \[j\]-th element of each of the term in as follows. First, we can write the first term as (bI - eta_x^(r+1)bA^(t)^topbA^(t))_(j,:)bx^(r) & = (1 - eta_x^(r+1)) bx_j^(r) - eta_x^(r+1)textstylesumlimits_i neq j langle bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_i ranglebx_i^(r). Next, the second term in can be expressed as eta_x^(r+1) ((bA^(t) - bA^*)^topbA^*)_(j,:)bx^* &= eta_x^(r+1)textstylesumlimits_i langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle bx_i^*\\ &= eta_x^(r+1)langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_jrangle bx_j^* + eta_x^(r+1)textstylesumlimits_ineq j langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle bx_i^*. Finally, we have the following expression for the third term, eta_x^(r+1)(bA^*topbA^*)_(j,:)bx^* &= eta_x^(r+1) bx_j^* + eta_x^(r+1)textstylesumlimits_i neq j langle bA^*_j, bA^*_i rangle bx^*_i. Now using our definition of \[lambda^(t)_j = |langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_jrangle| leq tfracepsilon_t^22\], combining all the results for , and using the fact that since \[bA^(t)\] is close to \[bA^*\], vectors \[bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\] and \[bA^*_j\] enclose an obtuse angle, we have the following for the \[j\]-th entry of the \[(r+1)\]-th iterate, \[bx^(r+1)\] is given by bx_j^(r+1) = (1 - eta_x^(r+1)) &bx_j^(r) + eta_x^(r+1)(1 - lambda^(t)_j) bx_j^* + eta_x^(r+1)xi^(r+1)_j . Here \[xi^(r+1)_j\] is defined as xi^(r+1)_j &:= textstylesumlimits_i neq j( langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle + langle bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle) bx^*_i -textstylesumlimits_i neq j langle bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle bx_i^(r). Since, \[langle bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle - langle bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle = langle bA^*_j, bA^*_i - bA^(t)_irangle + langle bA^*_j -bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle\], we can write \[xi^(r+1)_j\] as xi^(r+1)_j & = beta^(t)_j + textstylesumlimits_i neq jlangle bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle (bx_i^*-bx_i^(r)), where \[beta^(t)_j\] is defined as beta^(t)_j & := textstylesumlimits_i neq j (langle bA^*_j, bA^*_i - bA^(t)_irangle + langle bA^*_j -bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle + langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_irangle) bx_i^*. Note that \[beta^(t)_j\] does not change for each iteration \[r\] of the coefficient update step. Further, by Claim~ we show that \[|beta^(t)_j| leq t_beta = cO(sqrtkepsilon_t)\] with probability at least \[(1-delta_beta^(t))\]. Next, we define \[tildexi^(r+1)_j\] as tildexi^(r+1)_j & := beta^(t)_j + textstylesumlimits_i neq j|langle bA^(t)_j, bA^(t)_irangle| |bx_i^* - bx_i^(r)|. where \[xi^(r+1)_j leq tildexi^(r+1)_j\]. Further, using Claim~, tildexi^(r+1)_j &leq t_beta + tfracmu_tsqrtn \|bx^*_j - bx^(r)_j\|_1 := tildexi^(r+1)_max = tildeO(tfracksqrtn), since \[\|bx^(r-1) - bx^*\|_1 =cO(k)\]. Therefore, for the \[(r+1)\]-th iteration, we choose the threshold to be tau^(r+1) := eta_x^(r+1)tildexi^(r+1)_max, and the step-size by setting the ``noise'' component of to be smaller than the ``signal'' part, specifically, half the signal component, i.e., eta_x^(r+1)tildexi^(r+1)_max &leq tfrac(1 - eta_x^(r+1))2bx^(r)_min + tfraceta_x^(r+1)2(1-tfracepsilon_t^22)C, Also, since we choose the threshold as \[ tau^(r) := eta_x^(r)tildexi^(r)_max\], \[bx^(r)_min = eta_x^(r)tildexi^(r)_max\], where \[bx^(0)_min = C/2\], we have the following for the \[(r+1)\]-th iteration, eta_x^(r+1)tildexi^(r+1)_max &leq tfrac(1 - eta_x^(r+1))2eta_x^(r)tildexi^(r)_max + tfraceta_x^(r+1)2(1-tfracepsilon_t^22)C. Therefore, for this step we choose \[eta_x^(r+1)\] as eta_x^(r+1) leq tfractfraceta_x^(r)2tildexi^(r)_maxtildexi^(r+1)_max+ tfraceta_x^(r)2tildexi^(r)_max - tfrac12(1-tfracepsilon_t^22)C, Therefore, \[eta_x^(r+1)\] can be chosen as eta_x^(r+1)leq c^(r+1)(epsilon_t, mu, k, n), for a small constant \[c^(r+1)(epsilon_t, mu, k, n)\], \[eta_x^(r+1)\]. In addition, if we set all \[eta_x^(r) = eta_x\], we have that \[eta_x = tildeOmega(tfracksqrtn)\] and therefore \[tau^(r) = tau = tildeOmega(tfrack^2n)\]. Further, since we initialize with the hard-thresholding step, the entries in \[|bx^(0)| geq C/2\]. Here, we define \[tildexi^(0)_max = C\] and \[eta_x^(0) = 1/2\], and set the threshold for initial step as \[eta_x^(0)tildexi^(0)_max\].

nodes.statement: Since we only have access to the empirical estimate of the gradient \[hatbg_i^(t)\], we will show that this estimate is correlated with \[(bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j)\]. To this end, first from Lemma~ we have that the empirical gradient vector concentrates around its mean, specifically, \|hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t)\| leq o(tfrackmepsilon_t), with probability at least \[(1 -delta_bg_i^(t)- delta_beta^(t) - delta_cT^(t) - delta_HW^(t))\]. From Lemma~, we have the following expression for the expected gradient vector bg^(t)_j &= p_jq_j (bA^(t)_j- bA^*_j) + p_jq_j(- lambda^(t)_jbA^(t)_j+ tfrac1 p_jq_jDelta^(t)_j pm gamma). Let \[bg^(t)_j = 4rho_\_ (bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j) + v\], where \[4rho_\_ = p_jq_j\] and \[v\] is defined as v = p_jq_j(- lambda^(t)_jbA^(t)_j+ tfrac1 p_jq_jDelta^(t)_j pm gamma). Then, \[hatbg_i^(t) \] can be written as hatbg_i^(t) &= hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t) + bg_i^(t),notag \\ & = (hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t)) + 4rho_\_ (bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j) + v, notag \\ & = 4rho_\_ (bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j) + tildev, where \[tildev = v + (hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t))\]. Let \[\|tildev\| leq rho_\_\|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\| \]. Using the definition of \[v\] as shown in we have \|tildev\| leq q_j p_jlambda^(t)_j\|bA^(t)_j\|+ \|Delta^(t)_j\| + o(tfrackmepsilon_t) pm gamma. Now for the first term, since \[\|bA^(t)_j\| = 1\], we have \[lambda^(t)_j = |langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_jrangle| = tfrac12\| bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|^2\], therefore q_j p_jlambda^(t)_j\|bA^(t)_j\| = q_j p_jtfrac12\| bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|^2, Further, using Claim~ \|Delta^(t)_j\| & = O(sqrtmq_i,jp_i_1epsilon_t\|bA^(t)\|). Now, since \[ \|bA^(t) - bA^*\| leq 2\|bA^*\|\] (the closeness property (Def.) is maintained at every step using Lemma~), and further since \[\|bA^*\| = O(sqrtm/n)\], we have that \|bA^(t)\| leq \|bA^(t) - bA^*\| + \|bA^*\| = O(sqrttfracmn). Therefore, we have \|Delta^(t)_j\| + o(tfrackmepsilon_t) pm gamma = O(sqrtmq_i,jp_i_1epsilon_t\|bA^(t)\|). Here, we use the fact that \[gamma\] drops with decreasing \[epsilon_t\] as argued in Lemma~. Next, using , we have \|hatbg^(t)_j\| leq 4rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|+ \|tildev\|. Now, letting \|Delta^(t)_j\| + o(tfrackmepsilon_t) pm gamma = O(sqrtmq_i,jp_i_1epsilon_t\|bA^(t)\|) leq tfracq_ip_i2\| bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|, we have that, for \[k = cO (sqrtn)\] \|tildev\| leq q_ip_i\| bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|. Substituting for \[\|tildev\|\], this implies that \[\|hatbg^(t)_j\|^2 leq 25rho_\_^2 \|bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|^2\]. Further, we also have the following lower-bound langle hatbg^(t)_j, bA^(t)_j - bA^*_jrangle geq 4rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|^2 - \|tildev\| \|bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|. Here, we use the fact that R.H.S. can be minimized only if \[tildev\] is directed opposite to the direction of \[bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\]. Now, we show that this gradient is \[(rho_\_, 1/100rho_\_, 0)\] correlated, langlehatbg^(t)_i, bA^(t)_i - &bA^*_irangle - rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 - tfrac1100rho_\_\|hatbg^(t)_i\|^2, \\ &geq 4rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 - \|tildev\| \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\| - rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 - tfrac1100rho_\_\|hatbg^(t)_i\|^2, \\ &geq 4rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 - 2rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 -tfrac25rho_\_^2 \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2100rho_\_,\\ &geq rho_\_ \|bA^(t)_i - bA^*_i\|^2 geq 0. Therefore, for this choice of \[k\], i.e. \[k = cO (sqrtn)\], there is no bias in dictionary estimation in comparison to . This gain can be attributed to estimating the coefficients simultaneously with the dictionary. Further, since we choose \[4rho_\_ = p_jq_j\], we have that \[rho_\_ = Theta(k/m)\], as a result \[rho__+ = 1/100rho_\_ = Omega(m/k)\]. Applying Lemma~ we have \|bA^(t+1)_j- bA^*_j\|^2 leq (1 - rho_\_eta_A)\|bA^(t)_j- bA^*_j\|^2, for \[eta_A = O(m/k)\] with probability at least \[(1 - delta_cT^(t) - delta_beta^(t) - delta_bg_i^(t))\].

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:grad_mat}
nodes.statement: Here, we will prove that \[hatbg^(t)\] defined as hatbg^(t) = textstylesum_j (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top, concentrates around its mean. Notice that each summand \[(by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top\] is a random matrix of the form \[(by-bA^(t)hatbx)sign(hatbx)^top\]. Also, we have \[bg^(t)\] defined as bg^(t) = E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx)sign(hatbx)^top]. To bound \[\|hatbg^(t) - bg^(t)\|\], we are interested in \[\|sum_j=1^p bW_j\|\], where each matrix \[bW_j\] is given by bW_j = tfrac1p (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top- tfrac1p E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx)sign(hatbx)^top]. Noting that \[E[bW_j] = 0\], we will employ the matrix Bernstein result (Lemma~) to bound \[\|hatbg^(t) - bg^(t)\|\]. To this end, we will bound \[\|bW_j\|\] and the variance proxy v(bW_j) = max \\|textstylesum_j=1^p E[bW_jbW_j^top]\|, \|textstylesum_j=1^p E[bW_j^top bW_j]\| \. noindentBound on \[\|bW_j\|\]-- First, we can bound both terms in the expression for \[bW_j\] by triangle inequality as \|bW_j\| &leq tfrac1p \|(by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top\| + tfrac1p \|E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx)sign(hatbx)^top\|,\\ & leq tfrac2p\|(by-bA^(t)hatbx)sign(hatbx)^top\|. Here, we use Jensen's inequality for the second term, followed by upper-bounding the expected value of the argument by \[\|(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top\|\]. Next, using Claim~ we have that with probability at least \[(1 - delta_beta^(t) - delta_cT^(t) - delta_HW^(t))\], \[\|by-bA^(t)hatbx\|\] is \[siritildeO(kt_beta)\], and the fact that \[\| sign(x)^T\| = sqrtk\], \|bW_j\| &leq tfrac2psqrtk\|(by-bA^(t)hatbx)\| = siriO(tfracksqrtkpt_beta). noindentBound on the variance statistic \[v(bW_j)\]-- For the variance statistic, we first look at \[\|textstylesum E[bW_jbW_j^top]\|\], E[bW_jbW_j^top] = tfrac1p^2 E[(by_(j)-bA^(t)&hatbx_(j))sign(hatbx_(j))^top - E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top]\\ &times [sign(hatbx_(j)) (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) ^top -(E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top)^top]. Since \[bE[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top]bE[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top]^top\] is positive semidefinite, E[bW_jbW_j^top] preceq tfrac1p^2 E[(by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top sign(hatbx_(j)) (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j))^top]. Now, since each \[hatbx_(j)\] has \[k\] non-zeros, \[sign(hatbx_(j))^topsign(hatbx_(j)) = k\], and using Claim~, with probability at least \[(1-delta_cT^(t) - delta_beta^(t))\] \|textstylesum E[bW_jbW_j^top]\| &leq tfrackp \|E[(by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j))^top]\|, \\ &=O(tfrack^3t_beta^2pm)\|bA^*\|^2. Similarly, expanding \[E[bW_j^topbW_j] \], and using the fact that \[E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top]^topE[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) sign(hatbx)^top]\] is positive semi-definite. Now, using Claim~ and the fact that entries of \[E[(sign(hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top]\] are \[q_i\] on the diagonal and zero elsewhere, where \[q_i = O(k/m)\], \|textstylesum E[bW_j^topbW_j]\| &preceqtfrac1p\|E[(sign(hatbx_(j))(by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j))^top (by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)) sign(x^(R)_(j))^top]\|,\\ &leq tfrac1p\|E[(sign(hatbx_(j)) sign(hatbx_(j))^top] \| \|by_(j)-bA^(t)hatbx_(j)\|^2,\\ &leq siriO(tfrackmp) tildeO(k^2t_beta^2) = siritildeO(tfrack^3t_beta^2mp) . Now, we are ready to apply the matrix Bernstein result. Since, \[m = O(n)\] the variance statistic comes out to be \[O(tfrack^3t_beta^2pm)\|bA^*\|^2\], then as long as we choose \[p = tildeOmega(mk^2)\] (using the bound on \[t_beta\]), with probability at least \[(1 - delta_beta^(t) - delta_cT^(t) - delta_HW^(t) - delta_bg^(t))\] \|hatbg^(t) - bg^(t)\| &leq O(tfracksqrtkpt_beta) + \|bA^*\|sqrtO(tfrack^3t_beta^2pm),\\ &= O^*(tfrackm \|bA^*\| ). where \[delta_bg^(t) = (n+m)exp(-Omega(msqrtlog(n))\].

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:closeness}
nodes.statement: This lemma ensures that the dictionary iterates maintain the closeness property (Def.) and satisfies the prerequisites for Lemma~. The update step for the \[i\]-th dictionary element at the \[s+1\] iteration can be written as bA_i^(t+1) - bA _i^* &= bA_i^(t) - bA_i^* - eta_A hatbg_i^(t),\\ &= bA_i^(t) - bA_i^* - eta_A bg_i^(t) - eta_A (hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t)). Here, \[bg_i^(t)\] is given by the following as per Lemma~ with probability at least \[(1 - delta_cT^(t) - delta_beta^(t))\] bg^(t)_i &= q_i p_i (bA^(t)_i- bA^*_i) + q_i p_i(- lambda^(t)_ibA^(t)_i+ tfrac1q_i p_iDelta^(t)_i pm gamma). Substituting the expression for \[bg_i^(t)\] in the dictionary update step, bA_i^(t+1) - bA _i^* &= (1 - eta_A p_i q_i) (bA_i^(t) - bA_i^*) - eta_A p_i q_ilambda^(t)_i bA^(t)_i - eta_A Delta^(t)_i - eta_A (hatbg_i^(t) - bg_i^(t)) pm gamma, where \[Delta^(t)_j= bE[bA^(t)vartheta^(R)sign(bx^*_j)] _j\]. Therefore, the update step for the dictionary (matrix) can be written as bA^(t+1) - bA^* &= (bA^(t) - bA^*)diag((1 - eta_A p_i q_i)) + eta_A bU - eta_A bV pm gamma - eta_A (hatbg^(t) - bg^(t)), where, \[bU = bA^(t) diag(p_i q_ilambda^(t)_i) \] and \[bV = bA^(t) bQ\], with the matrix \[bQ\] given by, bQ_i,j = q_i,jbE_bx_S^*[vartheta^(R)_isign(bx^*_j)|S], and using the following intermediate result shown in Claim~, bE_bx_S^*[vartheta^(R)_isign(bx^*_j)|S] leq gamma^(R)_i, & ~for~ i = j, \\ = O(p_jepsilon_t ),& ~for~ i neq j, we have \[\|bQ_i\| = O(sqrtmq_i,jp_iepsilon_t)\]. Hence, we have \|bQ\|_F leq O(mq_i,jp_iepsilon_t). Therefore, \|bV\| leq \|bA^(t) bQ\| leq \|bA^(t)\| \|bQ\|_F = O(mq_i,jp_iepsilon_t \|bA^*\|) = O(tfrack^2m log(n)) \|bA^*\|. We will now proceed to bound each term in . Starting with \[(bA^(t) - bA^*)diag(1 - eta_A p_i q_i)\], and using the fact that \[p_i = O(1)\], \[q_i = O(k/m)\], and \[\|bA^(t) - bA^*\| leq 2\|bA^*\|\], we have \|(bA^(t) - bA^*)diag(1 - eta_A p_i q_i)\| &leq (1 - undersetimin~eta_A p_i q_i)\|(bA^(t) - bA^*)\| leq 2(1 - Omega(eta_A k/m))\|bA^*\|. Next, since \[\|bA^(t)_j\| = 1\], we have \[lambda^(t)_j = |langle bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j, bA^*_jrangle| = tfrac12\| bA^(t)_j - bA^*_j\|^2\], and \[lambda^(t)_i leq epsilon^2_t/2\], therefore \|bU\| &= \|bA^(t) diag(p_i q_ilambda^(t)_i) \| leq undersetimax~p_i q_itfracepsilon_t^22\|bA^(t) - bA^* + bA^*\| leq o(k/m) \| bA^*\|. Using the results derived above, and the the result derived in Lemma~ which states that with probability at least \[(1 - delta_beta^(t) - delta_cT^(t) - delta_HW^(t) - delta_bg^(t))\], \[\|hatbg^(t) - bg^(t)\| = O^*(tfrackm \|bA^*\| ) )\] we have \|bA^(t+1) - &bA^*\|= \|(bA^(t) - bA^*)bD_(1 - eta_A p_i q_i)\| + eta_A \|bU\| + eta_A \|bV\| + eta_A \|(hatbg^(t) - bg^(t))\| pm gamma,\\ &leq 2(1 - Omega(eta_A tfrackm) \|bA^*\|+ o(eta_A tfrackm)\|bA^*\| + O( eta_A tfrack^2mlog(n))\|bA^*\| + o(eta_Atfrack m \|bA^*\| ) pm gamma,\\ &leq 2\|bA^*\|.

nodes.statement: Let \[F_bx^*\] be the event that \[sign(bx^*) = sign(hatbx)\], and let \[mathbbm1_F_bx^*\] denote the indicator function corresponding to this event. As we show in Lemma~, this event occurs with probability at least \[(1 - delta_beta^(t) - delta_cT^(t))\], therefore, E[(by-bA^(t)&hatbx)(by-bA^(t)hatbx)^top] \\ &= E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^topmathbbm1_F_bx^*] +E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^topmathbbm1_barF_x^*], \\ &= E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^topmathbbm1_F_x^*] pm gamma. Here, \[gamma\] is small. Under the event \[F_x^*\], \[hatbx\] has the correct signed-support. Again, since \[mathbbm1_F_bx^* = 1 - mathbbm1_barF_bx^*\], E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^top] &= E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^top(1 - mathbbm1_barF_x^*)] pm gamma,\\ &= E[(by-bA^(t)hatbx) (by-bA^(t)hatbx)^top] pm gamma. Now, using Lemma~ with probability at least \[(1-delta_cT^(t) - delta_beta^(t))\], \[hatbx_S\] admits the following expression hatbx_S := bx^(R)_S = (bI - Lambda^(t)_S) bx^*_S + vartheta^(R)_S. Therefore we have by - bA^(t)hatbx &=(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bx^*_S - bA^(t)_Svartheta^(R)_S. Using the expression above \[bE[(by - bA^(t)hatbx)(by - bA^(t)hatbx)^top] \] can be written as bE[(by &- bA^(t)hatbx)(by - bA^(t)hatbx)^top] \\ &= bE[((bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bx^*_S - bA^(t)_Svartheta^(R)_S)((bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bx^*_S - bA^(t)_Svartheta^(R)_S)^top]. Sub-conditioning, we have bE[(by - bA^(t)hatbx)(by - &bA^(t)hatbx)^top]\\ = &bE_S[(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bE_bx^*_S[bx^*_Sbx^*^top_S|S](bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)] \\ &- bE_S[bA^(t)_SbE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_Sbx^*^top_S|S](bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)] \\ &- bE_S[(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bE_bx^*_S[bx^*_S(vartheta^(R)_S)^top|S]bA^(t)^top_S] \\ &+ bE_S[bA^(t)_SbE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_S(vartheta^(R)_S)^top|S]bA^(t)^top_S]. Now, since \[bE_bx^*_S[bx^*_Sbx^*^top_S|S] = bI\], \|bE[(by - bA^(t)hatbx)(by - bA^(t)hatbx)^top]\|notag &leq underbrace\|bE_S[(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))(bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)]\|_clubsuit \\ &~~~~+underbrace\| bE_S[bA^(t)_SbE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_Sbx^*^top_S|S](bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)]\|_spadesuit notag \\ &~~~~+underbrace\| bE_S[(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))bE_bx^*_S[bx^*_S(vartheta^(R)_S)^top|S]bA^(t)^top_S]\|_heartsuit notag\\ &~~~~+ underbrace\|bE_S[bA^(t)_SbE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_S(vartheta^(R)_S)^top|S]bA^(t)^top_S]\|_diamondsuit . Let's start with the first term \[(clubsuit)\] of , which can be written as clubsuit : leq underbrace\|bE_S[bA^*_S bA^*^top_S]\|_clubsuit_1 + underbrace\|bE_S[bA^*_S (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S]\|_clubsuit_2 &+ underbrace\|bE_S[bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^*^top_S]\|_clubsuit_3 notag \\&+ underbrace\|bE_S[bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S)^2bA^(t)^top_S]\|_clubsuit_4. Now consider each term of equation . First, since bE_S[bA^*_S bA^*^top_S] &= bE_S[textstylesumlimits_i ,jin S bA^*_i bA^*^top_j mathbbm1_i,jin S] = textstylesumlimits_i,j= 1^m bA^*_i bA^*^top_i bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S], and \[bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S] = O(tfrack^2m^2)\], we can upper-bound \[clubsuit_1:=\|bE_S[bA^*_S bA^*^top_S] \| \] as clubsuit_1:= \|bE_S[bA^*_S bA^*^top_S] \| = O(tfrack^2m^2)\|bA^* b1^m times m bA^*^top\| = O(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2, where \[b1^m times m \] denotes an \[m times m\] matrix of ones. Now, we turn to \[clubsuit_2:=\|bE_S[bA^*_S (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S] \|\] in , which can be simplified as clubsuit_2 leq \|textstylesumlimits_i,j =1^m bA^*_i bA^(t)^top_j bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S]\| leqO(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|\|bA^(t)\|. Further, since \[bA^(t)\] is \[(epsilon_t,2)\]-close to \[bA^*\], we have that \[\|bA^(t)\| leq \|bA^(t) - bA^*\| + \|bA^*\| leq 3\|bA^*\|\], therefore clubsuit_2 := \|bE_S[bA^*_S (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S] \| & =O(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2. Similarly, \[clubsuit_3 \] is also \[O(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2\]. Next, we consider \[clubsuit_4:= \|bE_S[bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S)^2bA^(t)^top_S]\| \] in which can also be bounded similarly as clubsuit_4 = O(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2. Therefore, we have the following for \[clubsuit\] in clubsuit:=bE_S[(bA^*_S - bA^(t)_S(bI - Lambda^(t)_S))(bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)] &= O(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2. Consider \[spadesuit\] in . Letting \[bM = bE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_Sbx^*^top_S|S]\], and using the analysis similar to that shown in , we have that elements of \[bM in R^k times k\] are given by bM_i,j = bE_bx_S^*[vartheta^(R)_ibx^*_j|S] leq O(gamma^(R)_i), & ~for~ i = j, \\ = O(epsilon_t),& ~for~ i neq j. We have the following, spadesuit:= bE_S[bA^(t)_SbE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_Sbx^*^top_S|S](bA^*^top_S hspace-3pt - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)] = bE_S[bA^(t)_SbM(bA^*^top_S hspace-3pt - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)]. Therefore, since \[bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S|S] = O(tfrack^2m^2)\], and \[\|b1^m times m\| = m\], spadesuit :=\|bE_S[bA^(t)_SbM(bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)&bA^(t)^top_S)]\|\\ &= \|textstylesumlimits_i,j = 1^m bM_i,jbA^(t)_i(bA^*^top_j - (1 - lambda^(t)_j)bA^(t)^top_j) bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S|S]\|,\\ &= O(epsilon_t)\|textstylesumlimits_i,j = 1^m bA^(t)_i(bA^*^top_j - (1 - lambda^(t)_j)bA^(t)^top_j) bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S|S]\|,\\ &= O(epsilon_t)O(tfrack^2m^2) (\|bA^(t)b1^m times m bA^*^top\| + \|bA^(t)b1^m times m bA^(t)^top\|),\\ &= O(epsilon_t)O(tfrack^2m) \|bA^*\|^2. Therefore, spadesuit:= \|bE_S[bA^(t)_SbM(bA^*^top_S - (bI - Lambda^(t)_S)bA^(t)^top_S)]\| siri = O(tfrack^2m) epsilon_t\|bA^*\|^2. Similarly, \[heartsuit\] in is also bounded as \[spadesuit\]. Next, we consider \[diamondsuit\] in . In this case, letting \[bE_bx^*_S[vartheta^(R)_S(vartheta^(R)_S)^top|S] = bN\], where \[bN in R^k times k\] is a matrix whose each entry \[bN_i,j leq |vartheta^(R)_i||vartheta^(R)_j|\]. Further, by Claim~, each element \[vartheta^(R)_j\] is upper-bounded as |vartheta^(R)_j| & leq siriO(t_beta). with probability at least \[(1 - delta_beta^(t))\]. Therefore, diamondsuit &= \|textstylesumlimits_i,j = 1^m bN_i,jbA^(t)_ibA^(t)^top_j bE_S[mathbbm1_i,jin S|S]\|= underseti,jmax |vartheta^(R)_i||vartheta^(R)_j|O(tfrack^2m^2) \|textstylesumlimits_i,j = 1^m bA^(t)_ibA^(t)^top_j\|. Again, using the result on \[|vartheta^(R)_i_1| \], we have diamondsuit:=\|bE_S[bA^(t)_SbNbA^(t)^top_S]\| = m~underseti,jmax |vartheta^(R)_i||vartheta^(R)_j|O(tfrack^2m^2) \|bA^(t)\|\|bA^(t)\| siri= O(tfrack^2t_beta^2m)\|bA^*\|^2. Combining all the results for \[clubsuit, ~spadesuit, ~heartsuit\] and \[diamondsuit\], we have, \|bE[(by - bA^(t)hatbx)(by - &bA^(t)hatbx)^top]\|\\ & = siriO(tfrack^2m)\|bA^*\|^2 + O(tfrack^2m) epsilon_t\|bA^*\|^2 + O(tfrack^2m) epsilon_t\|bA^*\|^2 + O(tfrack^2t_beta^2m)\|bA^*\|^2,\\ &=O(tfrack^2t_beta^2m)\|bA^*\|^2.

nodes.name: Matrix Bernstein \citep{Tropp2015}
nodes.statement: Consider a finite sequence \[bW_k in R^n times m \] of independent, random, centered matrices with dimension \[n\]. Assume that each random matrix satisfies \[bE[bW_k] = 0\] and \[\|bW_k\| leq R\] almost surely. Then, for all \[tgeq 0\], bPrbig\ \|textstylesumlimits_k bW_k\| geq tbig\ leq (n+m) expbig( tfrac-t^2/2sigma^2 + Rt/3big), where \[sigma^2 := max\\|textstylesumlimits_k bE[bW_kbW_k^top]\|, \|textstylesumlimits_k bE[bW_k^top bW_k]\|\\]. Furthermore, bE[\|textstylesumlimits_k bW_k\|] leq sqrt2 sigma^2 log(n+m) + tfrac13Rlog(n+m).

nodes.name: \citep{Arora15} Lemma 45
nodes.statement: Suppose that the distribution of \[bZ\] satisfies \[bPr[\|bZ\|geq L(log(1/rho))^C] leq rho]\] for some constant \[C>0\], then item If \[p = n^O(1)\] then \[\|bZ^(j)\| leq tildeO(L)\] holds for each \[j\] with probability at least\[(1 - rho)\] and, item \[\|bE[bZmathbbm1_\|bZ\|geq tildeOmega(L)]\| = n^- omega(1)\]. In particular, if \[tfrac1psum_j =1^p bZ^(j) (1 - mathbbm1_\|bZ\|geq tildeOmega(L))\] is concentrated with probability \[( 1- rho)\], then so is \[tfrac1psum_j = 1^pbZ^(j)\].

nodes.name: Theorem 40 \citep{Arora15}
nodes.statement: Suppose random vector \[bg^(t)\] is a \[(rho_\_, rho__+, zeta_t)\]-correlated with high probability with \[bz^*\] for \[t in [T] \] where \[T leq poly(n)\], and \[eta_A\] satisfies \[0 < eta_A leq 2rho__+\], then for any \[t in [T]\], bE[\|bz^(t+1)- bz^*\|^2] leq (1 - 2rho_\_eta_A)\|bz^(t) - bz^*\| + 2eta_A zeta_t. In particular, if \[\|bz^(0) - bz^*\| leq epsilon_0 \] and \[ zeta_t leq (rho_\_)o((1 - 2rho_\_eta)^t) epsilon_0^2 + zeta\], where \[ zeta = max_t in [T] zeta_t\], then the updates converge to \[bz^*\] geometrically with systematic error \[ zeta/rho_\_\] in the sense that bE[\|bz^(t+1) - bz^*\|^2] leq (1 - 2rho_\_eta_A)^tepsilon_0^2 + zeta/rho_\_.
